reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin packages and a team-based earning structure in which commissions depend on building a network and recruiting partners. It also encourages token purchases by presenting projected appreciation, including a claim that the price could increase fivefold in a year, while linking purchased tokens to participation in mining. The presentation is an instructional sales webinar for participation, not a warning or independent investigation.

citations.quote: When you are building a network, offering partners, it is much faster to earn your money.
cash should be obtained only for building a network
It is we sell packages, and we earn at the expense of recommendations.
price is going to increase 5 times a year and you make money doing it
package for example 1000 euros to get 10 thousand tokens

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly qualifies its projections instead of presenting returns as certain. It expressly acknowledges skepticism and says participants decide their own direction and assume risk. It also concedes that token prices may fall and that guarantees do not remain, while describing the growth scenario as only a forecast. Those qualifications matter: the speaker is discussing a speculative venture and inviting viewers to assess their own risk, not representing an assured outcome. The presentation even calls one future outcome potentially utopian and tells viewers to take on only the risks they choose. On this record, optimistic projections are conditional investment commentary accompanied by explicit uncertainty, not proof of deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Some people are still skeptical. It's your personal business, so everyone can choose their own direction. Everybody's taking on the risk on his own
theoretically, we have a good chance, it does not depend on us
Of course, this is maybe utopian. Who knows bitcoin better than anyone else does?
I am always a supporter of conservative scenario and forecasts

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited recruitment and package statements show that participation was discussed, but they do not erase the presentation's express risk disclosures. A projected increase is not a guarantee where the speaker separately says prices can fall and that no guarantees remain. The evidence therefore supports speculative commentary with warnings, not the conclusion that viewers were promised safe or certain profits.

then no guarantees are left
price is going to increase 5 times a year and you make money doing it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the central pitch. The same presentation tells viewers that a package can produce tokens, links returns to network building, and says the price will increase fivefold in a year. Calling the scenario conservative and acknowledging risk still leaves a concrete appreciation claim presented as a reason to participate; a disclaimer cannot make that sales message ordinary analysis.

opening.argument: The material is structured as a school and operational walkthrough of an exchange. Its title identifies a trading school, and the presentation explains exchange sections, order placement, mining displays, trading limits, order history, and how to use the interface. The speaker says the purpose is to make the information clear and promises practical instructions for placing buy and sell orders. That is consistent with an educational technology demonstration: viewers are being shown how a platform is organized and how its functions operate. The existence of promotional language within a tutorial does not change the dominant format into a scam; the supplied record does not independently establish that every forecast or business claim is verified or that the tutorial itself is a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: OneCoin School for Trading on the OneExchange!
Let's start trading. What do I need to know?
we will 2 make separate instructions show right how to place a application place order to buy or to sell tokens

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a school does not make the subject matter neutral. The tutorial explains how to buy tokens, wait through freezes, mine, and recover funds, while also discussing partner earnings and package sales. Those are actionable participation instructions, so the educational format functions as the vehicle for promotion rather than an independent demonstration.

citations.quote: we all who bought such packages so far we cannot sell it
the best way is waiting for the split then join coin mining
It is we sell packages, and we earn at the expense of recommendations.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational detail is precisely what makes the promotion actionable. The tutorial does not merely explain a generic exchange; it describes buying OneCoin tokens, mining them, waiting for splits, and earning through recommendations. Technical instructions can be educational in form while still directing viewers toward a recruitment- and purchase-based opportunity.

citations.quote: the best way is waiting for the split then join coin mining
When you are building a network, offering partners, it is much faster to earn your money.

opening.argument: The supplied material can be read as describing ordinary platform commerce: tokens are bought and sold through an exchange, with stated fees, limits, order durations, freezes, and cancellation procedures. It identifies a product, an interface, and operational terms rather than showing a guaranteed return, a required deposit to unlock an account, or a credential request. The speaker even explains that token prices can go down and that sales are limited to a percentage of the available balance. Referral language appears, but the excerpts do not establish a tiered matrix, a guaranteed downline income, or that every buyer must recruit others. The record therefore supports a contested commercial platform and referral arrangement, not a demonstrated scam mechanism.

The order can be open, not yet done, closed or expired

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a credential request is irrelevant to the actual allegations. The evidence expressly describes packages, token purchases, mining, and cash obtained through building a network. A scheme need not display a formal matrix or guarantee to be deceptive; the combination of paid participation, recruitment-based earnings, and promised appreciation is the mechanism at issue.

citations.quote: cash should be obtained only for building a network
package for example 1000 euros to get 10 thousand tokens
When you are building a network, offering partners, it is much faster to earn your money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The commercial details do not make the arrangement ordinary. The presentation says cash should be obtained only by building a network and says packages are sold for earnings from recommendations. It also presents token appreciation and mining as ways to recover or increase money. Those are affirmative indications of recruitment-based monetization, even if the transcript does not use the word matrix or promise an absolute guarantee.
